Messages.Author: lovre
Messages.Body:
Is a bleed announced together with conditioning, and then playing
grandest trick legal?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
lovre wrote:
> Is a bleed announced together with conditioning, and then playing
> grandest trick legal?

No. Conditioning cannot be played in the "as action is announced"
window.

Messages.Author: Ankur Gupta
Messages.Body:


Why? There is no card text preventing its use in this phase of the game.
Seduction seems to provide a limiting phrase only, not also simultaneously

Can reaction cards be played in that window once the acting Methuselah is
finished? Why or why not?

> Why? There is no card text preventing its use in this phase of the game.
> Seduction seems to provide a limiting phrase only, not also simultaneously
> an enabling phrase, for instance. Can action modifiers by default not be
> played in the "as action is announced" phase? If not, why not?

I think that we've just sorted this out on IRC with a logical explanation.
It kinda breaks down like this:

1. I PLAY the card "Govern the Unaligned" (with a window for as-played
effects)
2. I draw a card to replace Govern the Unaligned.
3. I ANNOUNCE "I am using the inferior dominate effect of this card".
4. I PLAY Seduction. (with a window for as-played effects for this card)
5. I draw a card to replace Seduction.
6. I PLAY The Sleeping Mind (with a window for as-played effects for this
card)
7. I draw a card to replace The Sleeping Mind.
8. Now that "as-announced" effects are over, this action is finished being
announced. After being announced, we now know that it is a Bleed Action.
9. I may play Conditioning.

Something like that.

Right?

Yes it's important to declare all the effects/terms of the card (other than
